transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in today?

Well... I suppose I'm just having a hard time shaking some thoughts. Even on my better days, I just... I get this feeling. 

It's mostly about some people at my church, and the walking club I go to. It just seems like they're... watching me. And... I don't know, putting little messages about me in the church bulletin. Or hiding things in what they say. That's... that's really why I'm here.
When your mood feels normal—not depressed or unusually energized—do these beliefs about people watching you still occur?

Yes... I suppose they do. There was a spell of several weeks not too long ago where I wasn't feeling so weighed down. I was actually getting dressed, eating a bit better... but, yes. I still thought the people at church were hinting about me. And... well, I'd still hear my name being called in the house.
How long have you been hearing your name called and believing that people at church are sending you messages?

Well... I suppose it's been a while. Maybe... about eleven months now. That's when I started noticing the messages, and... the voices. It's just... it's been hard to keep my thoughts straight since then.
During those eleven months, about how much of the time were you significantly depressed?

I suppose... most of it. The sadness, and... just feeling like I don't care much about anything... it's just sort of always there. Even when the voices aren't so loud, or the church people seem a bit quieter... I just... I still feel it. Most of the time, really.
During the several weeks when you were not feeling depressed, did you continue hearing your name and believing that people at church were sending messages about you?

Yes... I think I mentioned that already. Even when I was doing a little better... getting dressed and eating... I still heard it. And the church people, too. It didn't stop just because I felt less heavy.
